files_read: evidence/probe1_output.txt, evidence/probe2_output.txt, evidence/probe3_output.txt (non-warning lines, tails — to check whether any declared control failed; all three named controls report FIRED)
evidence/ directory listing (probe sources present but not read in full; the writeup is the prose)
symptom: A tracked item had stood for weeks as a temporary workaround waiting on a condition — retire this fallback once every story authors the time series it stands in for — and the waiting looked like ordinary pending work, because a wait-state produces no output that could look wrong. The condition could not be met, on two independent grounds, and one of the two was not recorded anywhere. Meanwhile the fallback was firing on more rows than the tracked model of it described, including rows inside stories the model treated as having outgrown it.
mechanism_as_described: Ground one: the population that would have to empty had no reason to empty. The authoring instruction in force explicitly directs authors NOT to produce the series unless the narrative specifically tracks change in that quantity, and the schema does not require it — so a story without the series is conformant, not deficient. The instruction predates the corpus rebuild, so the entire live corpus was generated under it, and the seven stories without the series are all of one structural kind, from two batches, three of them regenerated later under a stricter required-metrics schema and still without it. Under that instruction the wait-state never terminates by design. Ground two: even universal authoring would not have retired the fallback, because the series is sampled on a coarser grid than the other quantities and classification is evaluated at the union of all sample points. At a point where the other quantities have a sample and the series does not, the read falls through to the same fallback — 21 such rows across 10 stories that DO author the series, with the grids named per story (one at 0/6/12 against gap rows at 3/9, another at 0/20/40/50 against gap rows at 10/30, and so on). The two grounds are independent: closing either leaves the other standing.
detection_path: Neither ground came from re-reading the tracked item; both came from checking it against the substrate. The first was found by quoting the live authoring instruction and dating it — establishing it was in force before the corpus was rebuilt, which is what makes it govern every story rather than some. The second surfaced only from changing the denominator, and would have stayed invisible otherwise: counted per story, 39 author the series and 7 do not, which reads as steady progress toward the retirement condition; counted per row, 209 rows split into 162 taking the real path, 21 falling through inside series-authoring stories, and 26 in stories without the series — and the 21 is the whole second ground. Three per-process controls were fired and printed by name before the census was believed. A deletion counterfactual then measured the cost of acting on the tracked model: removing the fallback changes 16 of 46 timelines, collapses 7 of them to a no-verdict token entirely, and gives 9 more interleaved no-verdict rows that would surface downstream as phantom transitions.
consequence: The item could have been waited on indefinitely; no amount of the awaited work would have discharged it. The ruling reclassified the fallback from temporary to sanctioned, keeping a per-row provenance flag that marks which rows were supplied by it, and declined both alternatives on the measured costs. The counterfactual also showed that acting on the tracked model — deleting the fallback — would have re-created an error caught earlier by a different control, discarding real authored data behind a no-verdict token. A neighbouring concern in the same family was demoted from live to latent in the same pass: the two predicates whose divergence motivated it have zero consumers anywhere, established by a recursive search with a positive control rather than by an empty result alone.

extraction_notes.boundary_rule_applied: UNIT — prose REPORTS an instance. The document states a specific tracked item whose premise was contradicted by the live authoring instruction, names the date the contradiction began, and reports a second load-bearing path it says the item never recorded. Both are occurrences, each with a witness in the evidence directory; neither is a discussion of the concept.
extraction_notes.selection_rule_applied: One incident per directory, fullest DESCRIBED mechanism. I treated the false premise and the unrecorded second path as ONE incident rather than two, because the document itself frames them as the two grounds on which the same retirement condition fails, and splitting them would give two half-mechanisms where the prose gives one whole one. NOT extracted: (a) the finding that two predicates have zero consumers, which makes a tracked divergence risk latent — a declared absence with a controlled search behind it, not an instance of something reading as working while wrong; (b) the gap between 48 corpus entries and 46 classified stories, explained by two record-only files carrying no measurements — a denominator explanation the document supplies in passing; (c) the counterfactual's phantom-transition result, which is a predicted consequence of an action not taken, not an incident that occurred.
extraction_notes.redaction_note: Quantity names, predicate and file paths, category names, the tracker's identifier and dates-with-commit-hashes are stripped from the coder-facing fields. Grid examples, the 162/21/26 row split, the 39/7 story split, and the 16-of-46 counterfactual are retained: the contrast between the story-denominated and row-denominated counts IS the detection mechanism.

metadata.incident_location_note: The document is framed as a ruling that closes a tracked question, not as a defect report, but the incident is what the ruling is about — the findings section exists to establish that the tracked premise was false. Read as subject rather than incidental for that reason.
